subject: Proof of non-replication and ephemeral snapshot attestations for private deployment
messages:
From: Alice Bennett <alice@finexa.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:15:00Z
Subject: Customer request: proof of non-replication and ephemeral tenant snapshots

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. As we prepare internal sign-off for a private/VPC deployment at Finexa Health, our compliance team has two items we need explicit, evidence-backed answers for: 

1) Non-replication assurance: Will customer data (objects, snapshots, backups) ever be replicated outside the customer-designated region or to any Redwood-managed multi-region store? We need a short statement and the concrete artifacts you can provide to prove there was no cross-region copy.

2) Ephemeral snapshot deletion proof: For short-lived snapshots used by the runtime (for GC/rollback), what guarantees exist that a snapshot is purged within a defined TTL and is not restorable from provider-side snapshots (e.g., AWS EBS/Snapshot/Azure Managed Disk backups)? We'd like an attestation template and a sample evidence package (object manifests, deletion trail, KMS key access logs).

Can you confirm what you can provide and expected lead time? We aim to present to our security council on Friday (2026-12-10).

Appreciate it,
Alice
Alice Bennett
Head of Compliance, Finexa Health
alice@finexa.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Customer request: proof of non-replication and ephemeral tenant snapshots

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up-front: in our Private/VPC deployment model we do not replicate customer-controlled storage to Redwood-managed multi-region buckets unless explicitly configured by the customer. For ephemeral runtime snapshots we support an auditable deletion workflow that can be attested. Below I outline concrete artifacts and a proposed timeline.

What we can provide (artifact list):
- Storage mapping: a one-page diagram showing the customer-owned bucket/endpoint (S3-compatible) and the single-region binding for the tenant (vpc-data-matrix.pdf).
- Snapshot lifecycle export: CSV manifest of snapshot IDs, creation timestamps, TTL, and final deletion timestamp (snapshot-lifecycle.csv).
- Deletion trail: provider-side object deletion entries (S3 DeleteMarker/VersionId references) and internal tombstone records (s3-delete-trail.txt).
- KMS access logs for the key that encrypted the snapshot objects around the delete window (kms-rotate-logs.txt).

Key guarantees and mechanics:
- Non-replication: we bind the tenant to the customer-specified region and use customer-controlled storage endpoints. Our control plane keeps metadata references, but we do not copy objects to Redwood-managed multi-region stores. Any attempted cross-region replication requires an explicit config flag and entitlement.
- Snapshot TTL & purge: runtime snapshots are created on ephemeral storage and optionally exported to the customer bucket for assisted recovery. When exported snapshots are configured with a TTL, we run an automated purge job that: 1) deletes object references, 2) records delete markers/version removals, and 3) emits an audit event to the tenant's logging stream.
- Provider-level backups: we avoid provider snapshotting of the exported objects by default. If a customer asks us to take provider-managed snapshots for disaster recovery, those snapshots are explicitly recorded and included in the attestation package.

Proposed timeline:
- Draft attestation package (samples + template) in 3 business days.
- Full evidence package for a single canary tenant run in 7 business days (includes KMS logs and delete manifests).

I attached the high-level data map and a sample lifecycle CSV. Happy to run a canary attestation with your team.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Customer request: proof of non-replication and ephemeral tenant snapshots

Marissa / Rafael —

Working through this now. Technical clarifications and what I'll include in the package: 

1) Object vs. runtime cache: runtime KV caches (model state, KV cache) are in-memory and not part of the persistent export. Only exported artifacts written to the customer bucket are considered in the deletion attestation.

2) Proof-of-delete steps we will provide (scripted, reproducible):
   - List objects before deletion -> generate SHA256 fingerprints -> write manifest (manifest-before.csv).
   - Perform delete (S3 delete + versioned delete if enabled).
   - Capture provider delete markers and version IDs.
   - Record internal tombstone entry in our metadata DB with timestamps and operator id.
   - Query KMS audit logs for decrypt/encrypt/delete events in the timeframe.

3) Provider snapshot risk: For AWS-managed EBS/EFS-level backups, exported objects stored in customer-controlled S3 are not automatically snapshotted by the provider at the block layer for S3. For on-instance attached volumes we avoid long-lived snapshots by:
   - Not using provider block snapshots for exported objects by default.
   - If a customer requests provider-side snapshotting (rare), we record it and include explicit expiration policies and a signed acknowledgement that provider-level snapshots will exist.

4) Artifacts I'm attaching for the canary run (redacted): s3-delete-trail.txt (delete markers + version ids) and kms-rotate-logs.txt (KMS events). I'll also produce manifest-before.csv and manifest-after.csv and a short attestation template.

Edge cases:
- Versioned buckets: deletion markers vs object versions can make retrieval possible for a brief window until lifecycle policies run; we'll include lifecycle config snapshots and TTL proof.
- Glacier/Archive tiers: objects moved to deep archive complicate immediate purge; our default recommendation is to avoid tier transitions for attested artifacts.

I should have the first draft of artifacts by 2026-12-08.

Dev
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications for our council: 

1) Please include an explicit statement in the attestation that, by default, Redwood will not enable provider-level block or snapshot backups for exported artifacts unless Finexa explicitly requests it.

2) If Redwood does ever enable provider-side snapshots at our request, we want a maximum retention SLA (e.g., 30 days) and a notification window prior to snapshot creation. Can you confirm you can include that language?

If you can add those two items to the attestation template, we'll be comfortable moving to the next procurement step.

Best,
Alice
